v.why: With the 0->2 route removed, the direct 0->3 conv carries more of the signal.
A conv on 2->3 builds on the useful features a conv on 0->2 feeds into node 2.
Replacing a strong 3x3 conv with skip loses more than replacing other ops.
Node 1 holds learned features that a conv on 1->3 can refine.
Removing a strong conv from 0->1 costs more than removing a weak op.
Cutting 2->3 when 0->3 is already absent leaves the output nearly disconnected.
Adding any connection to the output gains most when the edge was empty.
Upgrading from skip gains less than filling an empty slot, because skip is already decent.
A conv on 1->2 only matters if node 1 carries informative features.
With no input to node 1, a pooling edge from node 1 carries nothing.

raw:
These hypotheses come from my prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 structure, not from querying the benchmark data. Convolutions on edges that connect to the output carry most of the accuracy. Edits that add a conv matter most when the cell would otherwise be poorly connected, and they matter less when a strong alternative path already exists.

1. Setting edge 3 (0→3) to nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 1 (0→2) is none. With the other route from the input weakened, the direct edge carries more of the signal.
2. Setting edge 5 (2→3) to nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 1 (0→2) is nor_conv_3x3. A conv on edge 1 feeds node 2 with useful features, so a conv on edge 5 can use them.
3. Setting edge 3 (0→3) to skip_connect helps less when edge 3 currently has nor_conv_3x3, because the edit then replaces a strong op with a weaker one. This is the case where the condition is the replaced op.
4. Setting edge 4 (1→3) to nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 0 (0→1) is nor_conv_3x3. Node 1 then holds learned features for edge 4 to refine.
5. Setting edge 0 (0→1) to none hurts more when edge 0 currently has nor_conv_3x3, since the edit removes a strong op.
6. Setting edge 5 (2→3) to none hurts more when edge 3 (0→3) is none, because the output node would be cut off.
7. Setting edge 3 (0→3) to nor_conv_1x1 helps more when edge 3 currently has none, since adding any connection to the output matters most there.
8. Setting edge 1 (0→2) to nor_conv_3x3 helps less when edge 1 currently has skip_connect. Skip is already a decent op, so the gain from upgrading it is smaller than from filling an empty slot.
9. Setting edge 2 (1→2) to nor_conv_3x3 helps more when edge 0 (0→1) is nor_conv_3x3. A conv on edge 2 only matters if node 1 carries informative features.
10. Setting edge 4 (1→3) to avg_pool_3x3 helps less when edge 0 (0→1) is none, because node 1 would have no input and the edge would carry nothing.
